questions.question: The Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the:
questions.explanation: The Vice-President chairs the Rajya Sabha.

questions.question: Which Indian city is known as the "Pink City"?
questions.explanation: Jaipur is known as the Pink City.

questions.question: The Thomas Cup is associated with which sport?
questions.explanation: The Thomas Cup is a men’s international badminton team event.

questions.question: The Western Ghats run parallel to which coast of India?
questions.explanation: The Western Ghats run along the western coast.

questions.question: The "Sun Temple" at Konark is located in which state?
questions.explanation: The Konark Sun Temple is in Odisha.

questions.question: NITI Aayog replaced which earlier body?
questions.explanation: NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission in 2015.

questions.question: Which planet has the most moons in the solar system?
questions.explanation: Saturn currently has the most confirmed moons in the solar system.

questions.question: Which vitamin is produced when skin is exposed to sunlight?
questions.explanation: Sunlight triggers Vitamin D synthesis in the skin.

questions.question: Which part of the plant conducts photosynthesis using the green pigment?
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll is the green pigment that captures light energy.

questions.question: The deficiency of which vitamin causes scurvy?
questions.explanation: Scurvy is caused by a deficiency of Vitamin C.

questions.question: Who was the first President of India?
questions.explanation: Dr. Rajendra Prasad served as the first President (1950–62).

questions.question: The ancient university of Nalanda was located in present-day:
questions.explanation: Nalanda is in present-day Bihar.

questions.question: The Nobel Prize is NOT awarded in which field?
questions.explanation: There is no Nobel Prize in Mathematics.

questions.question: Which day is celebrated as International Yoga Day?
questions.explanation: International Yoga Day is 21 June.

questions.question: How many bones are there in the adult human body?
questions.explanation: An adult human has 206 bones.

questions.question: The maximum strength of the Lok Sabha as per the Constitution is:
questions.explanation: The Constitution permits a maximum of 550 elected members in the Lok Sabha.

questions.question: Who administers the oath of office to the President of India?
questions.explanation: The Chief Justice of India administers the oath to the President.

questions.question: Which strait separates India from Sri Lanka?
questions.explanation: The Palk Strait separates India and Sri Lanka.

questions.question: Who gave the slogan "Give me blood and I will give you freedom"?
questions.explanation: The slogan is associated with Subhash Chandra Bose.

questions.question: Which festival is known as the "Festival of Lights"?
questions.explanation: Diwali is the Festival of Lights.

questions.question: NABARD is associated primarily with:
questions.explanation: NABARD funds agriculture and rural development.

questions.question: Which part of the Constitution deals with Fundamental Duties?
questions.explanation: Fundamental Duties are in Part IVA (Article 51A), added by the 42nd Amendment.

questions.question: The Simon Commission came to India in:
questions.explanation: The Simon Commission arrived in 1928 and was widely boycotted.

questions.question: Which is the smallest continent by area?
questions.explanation: Australia is the smallest continent.

questions.question: Which vitamin is essential for blood clotting?
questions.explanation: Vitamin K is required for blood clotting.

questions.question: Which river is the longest in the world?
questions.explanation: The Nile is generally regarded as the longest river in the world.

questions.question: Which element is essential for the formation of haemoglobin?
questions.explanation: Iron is essential for haemoglobin formation.

questions.question: In which sport is the term "googly" used?
questions.explanation: A "googly" is a type of delivery in cricket.

questions.question: How many chambers does the human heart have?
questions.explanation: The human heart has 4 chambers.

questions.question: Which gas is most abundant in the Earth’s atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen is about 78% of the atmosphere.

questions.question: The national animal of India is the:
questions.explanation: The Royal Bengal Tiger is India’s national animal.

questions.question: The process by which plants lose water through leaves is called:
questions.explanation: Transpiration is the loss of water vapour from leaves.

questions.question: The term "GDP" stands for:
questions.explanation: GDP = Gross Domestic Product.

questions.question: A money bill can be introduced only in the:
questions.explanation: A money bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha.

questions.question: The concept of "Directive Principles of State Policy" was borrowed from which country?
questions.explanation: The Directive Principles were borrowed from the Irish Constitution.

questions.question: The currency of Japan is the:
questions.explanation: Japan’s currency is the Yen.

questions.question: The headquarters of the United Nations is in:
questions.explanation: The UN headquarters is in New York City.

questions.question: Sound cannot travel through:
questions.explanation: Sound needs a medium and cannot travel through a vacuum.

questions.question: The Param Vir Chakra is awarded for:
questions.explanation: The Param Vir Chakra is India’s highest wartime gallantry award.

questions.question: Which is the highest mountain peak entirely within India?
questions.explanation: Nanda Devi is the highest peak entirely within India.

questions.question: The Davis Cup is associated with which sport?
questions.explanation: The Davis Cup is a men’s team tennis event.

questions.question: Which planet is known as the "Red Planet"?
questions.explanation: Mars looks red due to iron oxide on its surface.

questions.question: The "Right to Education" was made a fundamental right by which amendment?
questions.explanation: The 86th Amendment (2002) added Article 21A — Right to Education.

questions.question: The hardest natural substance known is:
questions.explanation: Diamond is the hardest known natural substance.

questions.question: If today is Wednesday, what day will it be after 55 days?
questions.explanation: 55 mod 7 = 6; Wednesday + 6 = Tuesday.

questions.question: Which letter is 8th to the right of the 13th letter from the left in the English alphabet?
questions.explanation: 13th letter = M; 13 + 8 = 21th letter = U.

questions.question: Find the odd pair: (4, 64), (9, 729), (5, 125), (2, 6)
questions.explanation: In each correct pair the second number is the cube of the first. 2³ = 8, not 6.

questions.question: In a row of 44 students, Ravi is 21st from the left. What is his position from the right?
questions.explanation: Position from right = 44 − 21 + 1 = 24.

questions.question: Find the next term: 49, 64, 81, 100, 121, ?
questions.explanation: These are perfect squares 7²…11². Next is 12² = 144.

questions.question: Find the next term: 4, 8, 14, 22, 32, ?
questions.explanation: Differences increase by 2 each step; next difference is 12, so 32 + 12 = 44.

questions.question: If TREE is coded as USFF, how is RAIN coded?
questions.explanation: Each letter is shifted forward by 1. Applying the same to RAIN gives SBJO.

questions.question: What is the angle between the hour and minute hands of a clock at 2:00?
questions.explanation: Each hour mark = 30°. At 2:00 the angle is 2 × 30° = 60°.
The relation is squaring: 4² = 16, so 6² = 36.

questions.question: If + means ×, and × means −, then evaluate: 9 + 5 × 6.
questions.explanation: Replace symbols: 9 × 5 − 6 = 45 − 6 = 39.

questions.question: Find the next term: 3, 10, 31, 94, ?
questions.explanation: Each term follows ×3 + 1: 94 × 3 + 1 = 283.

questions.question: Complete the series: B, F, J, N, ?
questions.explanation: Each letter advances by 4 places, so the next is R.

questions.question: Find the odd one out: 17, 10, 7, 11
questions.explanation: 11, 7, 17 are prime numbers; 10 is a composite number.

questions.question: Which letter is 4th from the right end of the English alphabet?
questions.explanation: The 4th letter from the right is the 23rd from the left = W.
The relation is cubing: 4³ = 64, so 2³ = 8.

questions.question: If today is Tuesday, what day will it be after 60 days?
questions.explanation: 60 mod 7 = 4; Tuesday + 4 = Saturday.

questions.question: Which letter is 2nd to the right of the 5th letter from the left in the English alphabet?
questions.explanation: 5th letter = E; 5 + 2 = 7th letter = G.

questions.question: Find the odd pair: (7, 343), (2, 8), (3, 26), (9, 729)
questions.explanation: In each correct pair the second number is the cube of the first. 3³ = 27, not 26.

questions.question: In a row of 32 students, Ravi is 15th from the left. What is his position from the right?
questions.explanation: Position from right = 32 − 15 + 1 = 18.

questions.question: Find the next term: 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, ?
questions.explanation: These are perfect squares 2²…6². Next is 7² = 49.

questions.question: Find the next term: 6, 10, 15, 21, 28, ?
questions.explanation: Differences increase by 1 each step; next difference is 8, so 28 + 8 = 36.

questions.question: If MOON is coded as NPPO, how is STAR coded?
questions.explanation: Each letter is shifted forward by 1. Applying the same to STAR gives TUBS.

questions.question: What is the angle between the hour and minute hands of a clock at 6:00?
questions.explanation: Each hour mark = 30°. At 6:00 the angle is 6 × 30° = 180°.
The relation is squaring: 5² = 25, so 6² = 36.

questions.question: What is 50% of 520?
Find the simple interest on ₹2500 at 5% per annum for 3 years.
Find the compound interest on ₹4000 at 5% per annum for 2 years.
An article costing ₹300 is sold for ₹360. Find the profit percentage.
An article costing ₹720 is sold at a 25% profit. Find the selling price.
Find the average of the first five multiples of 2.
questions.explanation: Multiples: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. Sum = 30. Average = 30/5 = 6.

questions.question: Two numbers are in the ratio 5 : 8 and their sum is 104. Find the larger number.
questions.explanation: Total parts = 13. Each part = 104/13 = 8. Larger = 8 × 8 = 64.

questions.question: A train 200 m long crosses a pole in 10 seconds. Find its speed in km/h.
A can do a work in 10 days and B in 40 days. Working together, in how many days will they finish it?
questions.explanation: Combined one-day work = 1/10 + 1/40 = 50/400. Time = 400/50 = 8 days.

questions.question: Find the area of a circle with radius 28 cm. (Use π = 22/7)
Find the value of √1600.
Find 20% of 20% of 1000.
Two numbers are in the ratio 4 : 7 and their difference is 27. Find the smaller number.
questions.explanation: Difference = 3 parts = 27, so each part = 9. Smaller = 4 × 9 = 36.

questions.question: A boat travels 39 km downstream in 3 hours. If the speed of the stream is 1 km/h, find the speed of the boat in still water.
questions.explanation: Downstream speed = 39/3 = 13 km/h = boat + stream. Boat = 13 − 1 = 12 km/h.
